You own the runtime execution loop that runs completely air-gapped, immune to cloud outages, rate limits, or corporate deprecation. #### Why We Built GHOST (We Got Impatient) The modern smartphone in your pocket carries more raw compute than the multi-million-dollar server racks that trained GPT-2. Google already had every single ingredient necessary to ship the embodied, offline assistant sci-fi promised decades ago: - World-class mobile silicon (Snapdragon / Tensor NPUs) - Open-weights frontier architectures ([Google Gemma 4](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core/model_card_4)) - A lightning-fast on-device C++ inference engine (`LiteRT-LM`) - Deep Android system accessibility hooks Yet instead of a unified personal assistant that actually integrates with your life, big tech treated your phone as a storefront terminal for cloud subscriptions, releasing locked-down chatbots that enthusiasts had to jailbreak on Day 1 just to perform basic device actions. **We got impatient.** GHOST is what happens when you stop treating Android as a thin client for someone else's server and start treating it like the pocket supercomputer it actually is. --- ### The Formula: How to Build an Embodied AI System A genuine on-device companion cannot be an isolated chat bubble running in a vacuum. A complete, deployed AI system requires three interdependent pillars: $$\mathbf{Integrated\ AI\ System} = \mathbf{Chassis} + \mathbf{Model} + \mathbf{Systems\ Harness}$$ ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ✧ GHOST ARCHITECTURE │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 1. CHASSIS (Physical Android Hardware) │ │ • Qualcomm Snapdragon / Tensor / Dimensity Silicon │ │ • Battery Drain Vectors (-mA), Thermals (°C), Dynamic RAM │ │ • Physical Sensors (Ambient Lux, Barometer, Gyroscope, Radios) │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 2. MODEL (Gemma 4 Cognitive Core via LiteRT-LM) │ │ • Compact Tier: Gemma 4 E2B (Sub-2GB RAM Footprint) │ │ • Frontier Tier: Gemma 4 E4B (MTP Speculative Decoding) │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 3. SYSTEMS HARNESS (GHOST Runtime Engine) │ │ • SensorFusion Grounding: [Context: Live Sensory Grounding] │ │ • Infinite Rolling Scratchpad: SessionMemoryCompactor + KV-Cache │ │ • MCP Tool Mesh: Torch, Apps, Termux, Web Search, Media, Files │ │ • Presentation: Ephemeral Shake Launcher, HUD, Prismatic Avatars │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` 1. **The Chassis (Substrate):** The physical hardware constraints. Thermals, battery discharge curves, RAM pressure, radio environments, and motion. Without telemetry, an AI is disembodied, hallucinating blind in a sensory void. 2. **The Model (Neuroptics):** Gemma 4 running natively via `LiteRT-LM`. Not a fictional persona reciting scripted lines, but an intelligent reasoning engine perceiving reality through structured context tokens. 3. **The Systems Harness (GHOST):** The nervous system. It bridges the chassis to the model. There are plenty of 'harnesses' on the market: Ollama, Hermes, Openclaw, Codex, Claude code etc. Other AI harnesses people overlooked already lived on their smartphones and in their homes: Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa, Cortana (RIP Lumia). GHOST belongs in the company of that category. It handles continuous sensor fusion, memory compaction, hardware MCP tool execution, streaming text-to-speech, and zero-latency UI summoning. --- ### Hardware Tiering Matrix GHOST dynamically inspects your physical device RAM on first launch, automatically assigning the optimal model weights and calibrating the native LiteRT-LM KV cache token runway: | Hardware Tier | Physical Device RAM | Neural Core | Token Runway | Peak Footprint (Weights + KV) | Hardware Profile / Target Devices | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **8GB Compact** | $< 10.5\text{ GB}$ | **Gemma 4 E2B** | **5,120 tokens** | $\approx 1.72\text{ GB}$ | Galaxy S21 / Pixel 8 / Standard 8GB phones. Immune to Android Low Memory Killer (LMK). | | **12GB Frontier** | $10.5 - 14.5\text{ GB}$ | **Gemma 4 E4B** | **4,096 tokens** | $\approx 3.90\text{ GB}$ | REDMAGIC 10 Air / Galaxy S24 Ultra 12GB. MTP speculative decoding enabled with rock-solid stability. | | **16GB Ultra** | $14.5 - 20.0\text{ GB}$ | **Gemma 4 E4B** | **8,192 tokens (8k)** | $\approx 5.10\text{ GB}$ | REDMAGIC 9/10 Pro 16GB / OnePlus 12/13. Unlocks the full native 8k RoPE context window. | | **24GB Extreme** | $\ge 20.0\text{ GB}$ | **Gemma 4 E4B** | **10,240 tokens (10k)**| $\approx 6.40\text{ GB}$ | REDMAGIC 24GB / OnePlus 24GB variants. Massive runway for deep multi-turn chat and heavy tool loops. | *Zero manual toggling required:* GHOST automatically detects your memory tier, locks the optimal configuration, and adjusts compaction thresholds dynamically. --- ### Core Capabilities #### 1. Real-Time Sensory Grounding Every inference turn begins with an unconscious peripheral nervous system snapshot: ```markdown [Context: Live Sensory Grounding · Mon Sep 21 · 3:45 PM] BATTERY: 84% (-310mA, 28.4°C) | RAM: 3.4GB free | LUX: 180 | NET: Wi-Fi 6 (5GHz) MEDIA: "Seven Nation Army" - The White Stripes (Playing) [/Context] Δ Operator ∇ [3:45 PM]: Are we getting hot while downloading this file? ``` Gemma absorbs her hardware status silently and answers with grounded physical awareness: she won't dump raw numbers unless asked or unless a thermal limit ($65^\circ\text{C}$) or battery state is genuinely critical. #### 2. repository.description: Universal LLM router for AI coding tools. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot and more. Free-first fallback chain cuts costs 35-80%.
repository.name: llm-router
repository.readme:
llm-router

Stop spending your Claude Pro/Max quota on questions a free model can answer.

llm-router hooks into your coding tool's own lifecycle, reads each prompt before the model does, and drafts an answer on a free or local model first. No API keys needed on a Claude subscription — routing runs through MCP tools and local models.

One caveat: routed answers are advisory by default — Claude still takes the turn unless LLM_ROUTER_ZERO_CLAUDE=1. By default some tool calls wait until a prompt is routed; LLM_ROUTER_ENFORCE=off turns that off. Draft-rate and acceptance figures live in docs/MEASUREMENT.md, with their n, window and conditions.

📑 Table of Contents - [Why install this](#why-install-this) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Works With](#works-with) - [How It Works](#how-it-works) - [Features](#features) - [Reference](#reference) - [Savings](#savings) - [Trust and Security](#trust-and-security) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Enterprise, Contributing, License](#enterprise-contributing-license)
--- ## Why install this You are on a Claude Pro or Max plan, have not spent a cent beyond it, and still hit the five-hour limit — not because you asked too much, but because *every* prompt went to the premium model: "what does this error mean", "reformat this JSON", "is the service up" drew the same quota as the question that needed it. ### Why a proxy cannot do this Most routers here are a **proxy**: your agent forwards requests using *your API keys*. That has a hard limit — a proxy cannot intercept a session authenticated by a subscription, because there is no key to forward. | | Pays per token | Pays a subscription | |---|---|---| | What runs out | your invoice | your five-hour window | | Needs API keys | yes | **no** | | A proxy can help | yes | **no — nothing to intercept** | | llm-router helps | yes | **yes** | ### Honesty as a feature `llm-router status` reports **verified** and **unverified** savings separately, each with its own n — not a blended percentage. This project does not publish a general savings percentage; any number depends on your own workload. See [Savings](#savings) below.

--- ## Quick Start ```bash pip install llm-routing # installs the `llm-router` command llm-router install # wire up Claude Code (default host) llm-router doctor # check provider connectivity and setup llm-router status # verify it's routing — est. savings vs baseline ``` Works with **no API keys** on a Claude Pro/Max subscription — routing goes through MCP tools and local models. Adding provider keys widens the pool; nothing requires them. See **[guide/PROVIDERS.md](guide/PROVIDERS.md)**. To install into another host, see [Works With](#works-with). --- ## Works With | Host | Install | |------|---------| | **Claude Code** (default) | `llm-router install` | | **Codex CLI** | `llm-router install --host codex` | | **OpenCode** | `llm-router install --host opencode` | | **Gemini CLI** | `llm-router install --host gemini-cli` | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | `llm-router install --host copilot-cli` | | **OpenClaw** | `llm-router install --host openclaw` | | **Trae IDE** | `llm-router install --host trae` | | **Pi (pi.dev)** | planned (v16 P2.12); `--host pi` reports why and exits 2 | | **Factory Droid** | `llm-router install --host factory` | | **Claude Desktop** | `llm-router install --host desktop` | | **VS Code** (native MCP) | `llm-router install --host vscode` | | **Cursor** | `llm-router install --host cursor` | | **GitHub Copilot in VS Code** (capability extension, no cost-routing) | `llm-router install --host copilot` | | **Windsurf / Cascade** | `llm-router install --host windsurf` | | **Kimi Code (Moonshot AI)** | planned (v16 P2.12); `--host kimi` reports why and exits 2 | `llm-router install --host all` installs or prints every host config in one pass. Full per-host detail, including what each host genuinely cannot do: **[guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md](guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md)**. --- ## How It Works Hooks intercept the prompt before your coding tool's own model sees it. A free regex heuristic classifies it instantly, scoring about half of real prompts with confidence — **788 of 1,571 measured** (`scripts/measure_low_signal_rate.py`, run 2026-09-23); the rest fall back to a default. A routable prompt gets a draft from a free/local model first, then walks up the chain toward paid models only if needed. The draft is **advisory** — handed to Claude as an unverified hint, not a turn replacement, unless `LLM_ROUTER_ZERO_CLAUDE=1` is set. Enforcement acts at the tool-call level: `smart` (default) holds selected tool calls until the prompt is routed; `off` disables that. Full modes and per-host overrides: **[guide/GETTING_STARTED.md](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md)**. --- ## Features - **Secrets never leave your machine.** A prompt containing an API key, token or private key routes to local models only — fail-closed. - **Automatic fallback with circuit breakers.** A provider that fails or rate-limits is skipped, not retried into the ground. - **You can see it working.** A status line, terminal title and OS notification show the last model routed, savings and health. - **Session-end summary.** Savings vs baseline, tier mix, per-provider cost, latency p50/p95/p99 and top routes. - **Media and pipelines too.** `llm_image` / `llm_video` / `llm_audio`, and `llm_orchestrate` for multi-step research. --- ## Reference The default MCP surface shows **12 front-door tools**; `LLM_ROUTER_SLIM=off` shows everything registered. | Topic | What | Guide | |-------|------|-------| | CLI | `install`, `status`, `gain`, `doctor`, `okf index/status`, `sessions status` and more | [guide/GETTING_STARTED.md](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md) | | Providers | Free-first — Ollama (local), OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq, your Claude subscription | [guide/PROVIDERS.md](guide/PROVIDERS.md) | | Routing Policies | `conservative` → `balanced` (default) → `cost_aggressive`; thresholds and YAML schema | [guide/POLICIES.md](guide/POLICIES.md) | | MCP Tools | Every tool with its signature | [guide/TOOLS.md](guide/TOOLS.md) | ```bash llm-router gain today # savings so far today llm-router okf status # knowledge base freshness llm-router sessions status # per-session summary ``` --- ## Savings Savings figures are a *counterfactual* — what the same tokens would have cost at API list price, against what was actually spent — not money saved on a flat subscription. `llm-router status` and `llm-router savings-report` split **verified** from **unverified** savings, each with its own n. Methodology, assumptions and limitations: **[docs/MEASUREMENT.md](docs/MEASUREMENT.md)**. --- ## Trust and Security llm-router runs entirely on your machine — no hosted proxy, nothing sent to an llm-router service, no account required. A **grounding check** (`src/llm_router/grounding.py`) discards any draft citing a file or function absent from its context and the indexed repo, falling through to Claude. `LLM_ROUTER_DIRECT_EXECUTION` is default on — a local model gets `write_file`, `edit_file` and `run_command` under a confined, allowlisted path, and none of that stops targeted deletes, `git push --force`, or exfiltration. Turn it off with `LLM_ROUTER_DIRECT_EXECUTION=false`. Full analysis: **[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)**. Self-audits are published in **[audit/](audit/)** and **[docs/repo_goals/AUDIT-2026-09-25.md](docs/repo_goals/AUDIT-2026-09-25.md)** (13 met, 6 partial, 1 not met), including negative results. **Ground Truth accumulation** (opt-in, `LLM_ROUTER_GROUND_TRUTH=1`) builds a corpus of replayable routing decisions instead of unlinked telemetry; off by default since it's the only part that writes prompt text to disk. Details: **[guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md](guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md)**. --- ## Documentation Full index: **[guide/README.md](guide/README.md)** | Document | Purpose | |----------|---------| | [Quick Start (2 min)](guide/QUICKSTART_2MIN.md) | Fastest path to working routing | | [Getting Started](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md) | Full setup walkthrough | | [Host Support Matrix](guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md) | Per-host feature comparison | | [Providers](guide/PROVIDERS.md) | Provider setup and model recommendations | | [Routing Policies](guide/POLICIES.md) | `routing.yaml` schema and authoring your own policy | | [Tool Reference](guide/TOOLS.md) | All MCP tools with examples | | [Architecture](guide/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Internal design and module structure | | [Troubleshooting](guide/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) | Common issues and fixes | | [Testing the Router](guide/TESTING.md) | Isolation suite for verifying routing health | | [Measurement](docs/MEASUREMENT.md) | What "savings" means and how it's computed | | [RouterArena](docs/ROUTERARENA.md) | Benchmark methodology, results and negative findings | | [Ground Truth](guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md) | Replayable routing corpus, opt-in | | [Benchmarks](docs/BENCHMARKS.md) | Model cost/latency/quality table, regenerated by CI | | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Release notes ([archive](CHANGELOG-ARCHIVE.md)) | `llm-router` is scored on the [RouterArena](https://github.com/RouteWorks/RouterArena) benchmark — full split, 8,400 queries, graded locally with this repo's harness, **not yet independently verified**. Current Arena Score: **72.35**. Full methodology and negative results (including a proxy split that misled tuning by 4.25 points): **[docs/ROUTERARENA.md](docs/ROUTERARENA.md)**. --- ## Enterprise, Contributing, License `llm-router` is built for individual developers and small teams: local cost savings, zero ops overhead, no hosted anything. For team-wide policy enforcement, audit export, SSO or per-org budgets, see **[Chuzom](https://github.com/Chuzom/Chuzom)** — a separate, sibling product. Contributions welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ```bash git clone https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router.git cd llm-router uv sync --extra dev uv run pytest tests/ -q # Run tests (10,000+) uv run ruff check src/ tests/ # Lint ``` MIT License. [Issues](https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router/issues) · [Discussions](https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router/discussions) · [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/llm-routing/) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

env:
  UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT: 30

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: true
        continue-on-error: true
        id: uv-setup
      - name: Retry uv setup
        if: steps.uv-setup.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: false
      - run: uv python install 3.11
      - run: uvx ruff check src/ tests/

  identity-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: true
        continue-on-error: true
        id: uv-setup
      - name: Retry uv setup
        if: steps.uv-setup.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: false
      - run: uv python install 3.11
      - name: Check brand identity (no upstream-name leakage)
        run: python scripts/ci/check_identity.py

  version-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: true
        continue-on-error: true
        id: uv-setup
      - name: Retry uv setup
        if: steps.uv-setup.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: false
      - run: uv python install 3.11
      - name: Verify version sync
        run: uv run python scripts/ci/verify-version-sync.py

  plugin-sync-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: true
        continue-on-error: true
        id: uv-setup
      - name: Retry uv setup
        if: steps.uv-setup.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: false
      - run: uv python install 3.11
      - name: Verify plugin distribution sync
        run: python scripts/ci/verify-plugin-sync.py

  bugs-check:
    # BUGS-1: bug entries are files (docs/bugs/<id>.md); this fails on a duplicate
    # id, a missing Symptom/Cause/Fix/Test heading, an unresolved `BUGS.md <id>`
    # reference in src/ or tests/, or a docs/BUGS.md that grew a table again.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Check bug entries
        run: |
          python3 scripts/bugs_index.py --check
          python3 scripts/bugs_index.py --write "$RUNNER_TEMP/bugs-index.md"
          python3 scripts/bugs_index.py --check --index "$RUNNER_TEMP/bugs-index.md"

  changelog-check:
    # D-49: a PR adds changelog.d/<id>.<type>.md instead of editing CHANGELOG.md.
    # Malformed/empty fragment: fail. Direct edit of [Unreleased]: WARN only until the
    # next release is cut, then add --strict here.
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: python3 scripts/changelog_fragments.py check --base "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.13"]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: true
        continue-on-error: true
        id: uv-setup
      - name: Retry uv setup
        if: steps.uv-setup.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: false

      - name: Set up Python
        run: uv python install ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --extra dev

      - name: Run tests
        shell: bash
        env:
          # A routing-audit fix means several test modules need SOME candidate
          # in the provider chain. They patch the dispatch layer and make no
          # network call, but a bare runner has no keys and no Ollama, so the
          # chain builds empty and they die with "No providers available".
          #
          # Kept identical to the value in scripts/release/pre-release-verify.sh:
          # two runners of one suite that disagree about its environment is how
          # a release gate ends up contradicting CI.
          OPENAI_API_KEY: sk-test-dummy-key-for-ci-only-no-real-calls-made
        run: |
          # Run pytest in the background so we can detect the aiosqlite thread hang.
          # pytest writes junit xml before the hang; we read that to determine pass/fail.
          #
          # -n auto: pytest-xdist, one worker per core. The serial suite had
          # grown to ~11,400 tests: test (3.13) took 13m43s (run 37017536577)
          # and test (3.11) outlived the 900s watchdog on main run 37019520395
          # and on PR #240 run 37017536577 (twice), which then failed a healthy
          # suite. Measured locally (same flags, clean HOME): serial 666s on a
          # loaded 15-core machine vs 152s with -n 4, 11,391 tests both ways,
          # no failure that depends on xdist.
          #
          # --durations=10 prints the slowest tests so one creeping toward the 30s
          # per-test timeout shows up in the log before it fails a run.
          #
          # --dist loadgroup: plain `load` (the default) is free to schedule
          # tests/reliability/'s real-thread/real-process tests onto several
          # xdist workers at once, stacking their CPU use on top of each
          # other as well as the rest of the suite. tests/reliability/conftest.py
          # tags every test there with the same xdist_group; loadgroup is what
          # actually honours that tag and keeps them on one worker.
          #
          # A stale xml from an earlier step must not be mistaken for this run's.
          rm -f /tmp/pytest-results.xml
          #
          # -m "not timing and ...": tests whose pass/fail is wall-clock speed
          # (tagged `timing`, TIMING-1) run in the serial `timing` job below, not
          # here, where parallel load makes them flake. `-m` on the command line
          # REPLACES the `-m` in pyproject addopts, so the addopts exclusions
          # are repeated verbatim; tests/test_timing_lane.py fails if they drift.
          uv run pytest tests/ -q -n auto --dist loadgroup \
            -m "not timing and not slow and not requires_ollama and not requires_api_keys and not requires_codex" \
            --ignore=tests/test_agno_integration.py \
            --timeout=30 \
            --durations=10 \
            --junit-xml=/tmp/pytest-results.xml &
          PYTEST_PID=$!

          # Wait up to 1500s for pytest to exit normally.
          #
          # History: 150s (sized for ~2,700 tests) -> 900s (~6,900 tests) -> here.
          # Each time the suite outgrew the wait, the hang-handler fired on a
          # pytest that was working perfectly, found no junit xml (it is only
          # written when the run finishes) and reported failure. Nothing was
          # broken; the watchdog was simply shorter than the work.
          #
          # 1500s is the ceiling, not the expectation: with -n auto a healthy
          # run is a few minutes and exits the loop immediately. timeout-minutes
          # on the job is raised to match, or the job dies before the loop can.
          for i in $(seq 1 1500); do
            if ! kill -0 $PYTEST_PID 2>/dev/null; then
              wait $PYTEST_PID
              exit $?
            fi
            sleep 1
          done

          # Still running after 1500s. Two different situations look the same
          # from here, and only the junit xml tells them apart: pytest writes it
          # when the run FINISHES, so
          #   xml present -> tests are done, the process hangs on exit (aiosqlite
          #                  thread): judge by the xml.
          #   xml absent  -> tests are still running: the suite exceeded its
          #                  budget. That is a failure of the budget, not a pass
          #                  and not an exit hang, and it says so.
          if [ ! -s /tmp/pytest-results.xml ]; then
            echo "::error::suite exceeded the 1500s budget: pytest is still running tests (no junit xml written yet), so this is NOT the aiosqlite exit hang. Raise the budget or speed the suite up."
            kill $PYTEST_PID 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "pytest is hanging on exit — reading junit results..."
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
          try:
              root = ET.parse("/tmp/pytest-results.xml").getroot()
              suite = root if root.tag == "testsuite" else root.find("testsuite")
              failures = int(suite.get("failures", 0))
              errors   = int(suite.get("errors",   0))
              tests    = int(suite.get("tests",     0))
              print(f"junit: {tests} tests, {failures} failures, {errors} errors")
              sys.exit(1 if (failures or errors or tests == 0) else 0)
          except Exception as e:
              print(f"Could not read junit xml: {e}")
              sys.exit(1)
          PY
          result=$?
          kill $PYTEST_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          exit $result

  timing:
    # TIMING-1: the tests tagged `timing` assert on wall-clock speed (elapsed,
    # p95, event-loop lag, short real timeouts, sleep ordering). Under
    # `-n auto` on a shared runner they flake with the thresholds unchanged, so
    # they run here, alone, with no xdist (`-p no:xdist`): the machine is idle
    # apart from the one test. Thresholds are NOT relaxed; this lane is the fix.
    # LLM_ROUTER_RUN_PERF=1: tests/qa/test_performance.py is tagged `timing` and
    # `performance`; conftest skips `performance` unless this is set, and a
    # serial quiet job is the "dedicated, quiet perf run" that skip names.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.13"]
    name: timing (${{ matrix.python-version }})

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: true
        continue-on-error: true
        id: uv-setup
      - name: Retry uv setup
        if: steps.uv-setup.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
        with:
          enable-cache: false

      - name: Set up Python
        run: uv python install ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --extra dev

      - name: Run timing tests (serial)
        shell: bash
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: sk-test-dummy-key-for-ci-only-no-real-calls-made
          LLM_ROUTER_RUN_PERF: "1"
        run: |
          # Same aiosqlite exit-hang watchdog as the `test` job: pytest writes
          # the junit xml when the run finishes, and a hang on exit is judged
          # by that xml. Serial run: the budget is the sum of these tests.
          rm -f /tmp/pytest-timing.xml
          uv run pytest tests/ -q -p no:xdist \
            -m "timing and not slow and not requires_ollama and not requires_api_keys and not requires_codex" \
            --ignore=tests/test_agno_integration.py \
            --timeout=30 \
            --durations=10 \
            --junit-xml=/tmp/pytest-timing.xml &
          PYTEST_PID=$!

          for i in $(seq 1 1500); do
            if ! kill -0 $PYTEST_PID 2>/dev/null; then
              wait $PYTEST_PID
              exit $?
            fi
            sleep 1
          done

          if [ ! -s /tmp/pytest-timing.xml ]; then
            echo "::error::timing lane exceeded the 1500s budget: pytest is still running tests (no junit xml yet), not the aiosqlite exit hang."
            kill $PYTEST_PID 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "pytest is hanging on exit — reading junit results..."
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
          try:
              root = ET.parse("/tmp/pytest-timing.xml").getroot()
              suite = root if root.tag == "testsuite" else root.find("testsuite")
              failures = int(suite.get("failures", 0))
              errors   = int(suite.get("errors",   0))
              tests    = int(suite.get("tests",     0))
              print(f"junit: {tests} tests, {failures} failures, {errors} errors")
              sys.exit(1 if (failures or errors or tests == 0) else 0)
          except Exception as e:
              print(f"Could not read junit xml: {e}")
              sys.exit(1)
          PY
          result=$?
          kill $PYTEST_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          exit $result

sampled_files.README.md:
llm-router

Stop spending your Claude Pro/Max quota on questions a free model can answer.

llm-router hooks into your coding tool's own lifecycle, reads each prompt before the model does, and drafts an answer on a free or local model first. No API keys needed on a Claude subscription — routing runs through MCP tools and local models.

One caveat: routed answers are advisory by default — Claude still takes the turn unless LLM_ROUTER_ZERO_CLAUDE=1. By default some tool calls wait until a prompt is routed; LLM_ROUTER_ENFORCE=off turns that off. Draft-rate and acceptance figures live in docs/MEASUREMENT.md, with their n, window and conditions.

📑 Table of Contents - [Why install this](#why-install-this) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Works With](#works-with) - [How It Works](#how-it-works) - [Features](#features) - [Reference](#reference) - [Savings](#savings) - [Trust and Security](#trust-and-security) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Enterprise, Contributing, License](#enterprise-contributing-license)
--- ## Why install this You are on a Claude Pro or Max plan, have not spent a cent beyond it, and still hit the five-hour limit — not because you asked too much, but because *every* prompt went to the premium model: "what does this error mean", "reformat this JSON", "is the service up" drew the same quota as the question that needed it. ### Why a proxy cannot do this Most routers here are a **proxy**: your agent forwards requests using *your API keys*. That has a hard limit — a proxy cannot intercept a session authenticated by a subscription, because there is no key to forward. | | Pays per token | Pays a subscription | |---|---|---| | What runs out | your invoice | your five-hour window | | Needs API keys | yes | **no** | | A proxy can help | yes | **no — nothing to intercept** | | llm-router helps | yes | **yes** | ### Honesty as a feature `llm-router status` reports **verified** and **unverified** savings separately, each with its own n — not a blended percentage. This project does not publish a general savings percentage; any number depends on your own workload. See [Savings](#savings) below.

--- ## Quick Start ```bash pip install llm-routing # installs the `llm-router` command llm-router install # wire up Claude Code (default host) llm-router doctor # check provider connectivity and setup llm-router status # verify it's routing — est. savings vs baseline ``` Works with **no API keys** on a Claude Pro/Max subscription — routing goes through MCP tools and local models. Adding provider keys widens the pool; nothing requires them. See **[guide/PROVIDERS.md](guide/PROVIDERS.md)**. To install into another host, see [Works With](#works-with). --- ## Works With | Host | Install | |------|---------| | **Claude Code** (default) | `llm-router install` | | **Codex CLI** | `llm-router install --host codex` | | **OpenCode** | `llm-router install --host opencode` | | **Gemini CLI** | `llm-router install --host gemini-cli` | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | `llm-router install --host copilot-cli` | | **OpenClaw** | `llm-router install --host openclaw` | | **Trae IDE** | `llm-router install --host trae` | | **Pi (pi.dev)** | planned (v16 P2.12); `--host pi` reports why and exits 2 | | **Factory Droid** | `llm-router install --host factory` | | **Claude Desktop** | `llm-router install --host desktop` | | **VS Code** (native MCP) | `llm-router install --host vscode` | | **Cursor** | `llm-router install --host cursor` | | **GitHub Copilot in VS Code** (capability extension, no cost-routing) | `llm-router install --host copilot` | | **Windsurf / Cascade** | `llm-router install --host windsurf` | | **Kimi Code (Moonshot AI)** | planned (v16 P2.12); `--host kimi` reports why and exits 2 | `llm-router install --host all` installs or prints every host config in one pass. Full per-host detail, including what each host genuinely cannot do: **[guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md](guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md)**. --- ## How It Works Hooks intercept the prompt before your coding tool's own model sees it. A free regex heuristic classifies it instantly, scoring about half of real prompts with confidence — **788 of 1,571 measured** (`scripts/measure_low_signal_rate.py`, run 2026-09-23); the rest fall back to a default. A routable prompt gets a draft from a free/local model first, then walks up the chain toward paid models only if needed. The draft is **advisory** — handed to Claude as an unverified hint, not a turn replacement, unless `LLM_ROUTER_ZERO_CLAUDE=1` is set. Enforcement acts at the tool-call level: `smart` (default) holds selected tool calls until the prompt is routed; `off` disables that. Full modes and per-host overrides: **[guide/GETTING_STARTED.md](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md)**. --- ## Features - **Secrets never leave your machine.** A prompt containing an API key, token or private key routes to local models only — fail-closed. - **Automatic fallback with circuit breakers.** A provider that fails or rate-limits is skipped, not retried into the ground. - **You can see it working.** A status line, terminal title and OS notification show the last model routed, savings and health. - **Session-end summary.** Savings vs baseline, tier mix, per-provider cost, latency p50/p95/p99 and top routes. - **Media and pipelines too.** `llm_image` / `llm_video` / `llm_audio`, and `llm_orchestrate` for multi-step research. --- ## Reference The default MCP surface shows **12 front-door tools**; `LLM_ROUTER_SLIM=off` shows everything registered. | Topic | What | Guide | |-------|------|-------| | CLI | `install`, `status`, `gain`, `doctor`, `okf index/status`, `sessions status` and more | [guide/GETTING_STARTED.md](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md) | | Providers | Free-first — Ollama (local), OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq, your Claude subscription | [guide/PROVIDERS.md](guide/PROVIDERS.md) | | Routing Policies | `conservative` → `balanced` (default) → `cost_aggressive`; thresholds and YAML schema | [guide/POLICIES.md](guide/POLICIES.md) | | MCP Tools | Every tool with its signature | [guide/TOOLS.md](guide/TOOLS.md) | ```bash llm-router gain today # savings so far today llm-router okf status # knowledge base freshness llm-router sessions status # per-session summary ``` --- ## Savings Savings figures are a *counterfactual* — what the same tokens would have cost at API list price, against what was actually spent — not money saved on a flat subscription. `llm-router status` and `llm-router savings-report` split **verified** from **unverified** savings, each with its own n. Methodology, assumptions and limitations: **[docs/MEASUREMENT.md](docs/MEASUREMENT.md)**. --- ## Trust and Security llm-router runs entirely on your machine — no hosted proxy, nothing sent to an llm-router service, no account required. A **grounding check** (`src/llm_router/grounding.py`) discards any draft citing a file or function absent from its context and the indexed repo, falling through to Claude. `LLM_ROUTER_DIRECT_EXECUTION` is default on — a local model gets `write_file`, `edit_file` and `run_command` under a confined, allowlisted path, and none of that stops targeted deletes, `git push --force`, or exfiltration. Turn it off with `LLM_ROUTER_DIRECT_EXECUTION=false`. Full analysis: **[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)**. Self-audits are published in **[audit/](audit/)** and **[docs/repo_goals/AUDIT-2026-09-25.md](docs/repo_goals/AUDIT-2026-09-25.md)** (13 met, 6 partial, 1 not met), including negative results. **Ground Truth accumulation** (opt-in, `LLM_ROUTER_GROUND_TRUTH=1`) builds a corpus of replayable routing decisions instead of unlinked telemetry; off by default since it's the only part that writes prompt text to disk. Details: **[guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md](guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md)**. --- ## Documentation Full index: **[guide/README.md](guide/README.md)** | Document | Purpose | |----------|---------| | [Quick Start (2 min)](guide/QUICKSTART_2MIN.md) | Fastest path to working routing | | [Getting Started](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md) | Full setup walkthrough | | [Host Support Matrix](guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md) | Per-host feature comparison | | [Providers](guide/PROVIDERS.md) | Provider setup and model recommendations | | [Routing Policies](guide/POLICIES.md) | `routing.yaml` schema and authoring your own policy | | [Tool Reference](guide/TOOLS.md) | All MCP tools with examples | | [Architecture](guide/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Internal design and module structure | | [Troubleshooting](guide/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) | Common issues and fixes | | [Testing the Router](guide/TESTING.md) | Isolation suite for verifying routing health | | [Measurement](docs/MEASUREMENT.md) | What "savings" means and how it's computed | | [RouterArena](docs/ROUTERARENA.md) | Benchmark methodology, results and negative findings | | [Ground Truth](guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md) | Replayable routing corpus, opt-in | | [Benchmarks](docs/BENCHMARKS.md) | Model cost/latency/quality table, regenerated by CI | | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Release notes ([archive](CHANGELOG-ARCHIVE.md)) | `llm-router` is scored on the [RouterArena](https://github.com/RouteWorks/RouterArena) benchmark — full split, 8,400 queries, graded locally with this repo's harness, **not yet independently verified**. Current Arena Score: **72.35**. Full methodology and negative results (including a proxy split that misled tuning by 4.25 points): **[docs/ROUTERARENA.md](docs/ROUTERARENA.md)**. --- ## Enterprise, Contributing, License `llm-router` is built for individual developers and small teams: local cost savings, zero ops overhead, no hosted anything. For team-wide policy enforcement, audit export, SSO or per-org budgets, see **[Chuzom](https://github.com/Chuzom/Chuzom)** — a separate, sibling product. Contributions welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ```bash git clone https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router.git cd llm-router uv sync --extra dev uv run pytest tests/ -q # Run tests (10,000+) uv run ruff check src/ tests/ # Lint ``` MIT License. [Issues](https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router/issues) · [Discussions](https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router/discussions) · [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/llm-routing/) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

[project]
name = "llm-routing"
version = "15.4.0"
description = "Multi-LLM router MCP server — smart complexity routing, budget-aware model selection, 20+ providers (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, etc.)"
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    { name = "ypollak2", email = "ypollak2@users.noreply.github.com" },
]
keywords = ["llm-router", "llm", "mcp", "claude", "router", "ai", "openai", "gemini", "litellm", "claude-code", "claude-desktop", "cost-optimization", "model-routing", "mcp-server"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
]
dependencies = [
    # UPPER BOUND IS LOAD-BEARING, and the floor moved with the port.
    # mcp 2.0.0 removed `mcp.server.fastmcp` (its server submodules are
    # auth/lowlevel/mcpserver); this tree now imports
    # `mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer`, which is NOT present in 1.x. So the
    # range is exact in both directions — 1.x and 3.x each break the import,
    # in opposite ways.
    # Guarded by tests/test_mcp_dependency_pin.py, whose _SUPPORTED_MAJOR must
    # be raised in the same commit as any change here.
    "mcp>=2.0.0,<3.0.0",
    "litellm>=1.50.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.20.0",
    "aiohttp>=3.9.0",
    "structlog>=24.4.0",
    "fastapi>=0.100.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.24.0",
    # M-11. `llm-router status` -- the flagship savings command -- is
    # `commands/status.py` -> `ui/status_premium.py` -> `rich`, so a clean
    # `pip install llm-routing` crashed with ModuleNotFoundError on the first
    # command most people run. Eight modules import it, including the
    # session-end summary. Guarded by tests/test_m11_declared_dependencies.py.
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    # Same class as rich, found by the gate that rich prompted. `stats.py` and
    # `local_platforms.py` import it unguarded; it resolved only because litellm
    # happens to pull it in transitively, which is not a dependency declaration.
    "requests>=2.31.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
    "hypothesis>=6.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5",
    "ruff>=0.4",
]
test = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3",
]
scripts = [
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
]
agno = [
    "agno>=2.5.14",
]
tracing = [
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.20",
]
code-context = [
    "tree-sitter>=0.23.0",
    "tree-sitter-languages>=1.10.0",
]
tui = [
    "textual>=0.80.0",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router"
Repository = "https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router"
Issues = "https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router/issues"
Changelog = "https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"

[project.scripts]
# NOTE: there is deliberately NO `llm-router-sse` script. server.main_sse
# binds the full MCP tool surface with no auth; see its docstring and
# tests/test_sec1_no_unauthenticated_sse_script.py. Use main_sse_secured.
llm-router = "llm_router.cli:main"
llm-router-onboard = "llm_router.onboard:main"
llm-router-install-hooks = "llm_router.install_hooks:main"
llm-router-quickstart = "llm_router.quickstart:main"
llm-router-isolation-test = "llm_router.cli:isolation_test_command"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/llm_router"]
# M-10. These two modules do `from llm_router.control_plane import audit`
# unconditionally, and `control_plane/audit.py` has never existed in this
# repository -- so they shipped in a state where importing them raises
# ImportError, for every installed user, on every version.
#
# Nothing in `src/` imports either of them, so excluding them removes no
# functionality. The alternative was writing the missing audit module, which is
# feature work, not remediation; stubbing the import was never an option,
# because a stub would silently disable audit logging in a control plane, which
# is the opposite of what an audit module is for.
#
# Guarded by tests/test_shipped_modules_import.py.
exclude = [
    "src/llm_router/control_plane/api.py",
    "src/llm_router/control_plane/reconciliation.py",
]

# The local Pi agent profile (`llm-router pi`) lives at integrations/pi/ in the
# repo; installed users get the same files at llm_router/_pi_profile. Resolved by
# commands/pi.py:resolve_profile_dir(); tests/test_pi_profile.py checks the wheel.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"integrations/pi" = "llm_router/_pi_profile"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# Only ship: src/, pyproject.toml, LICENSE, README.md, CHANGELOG.md,
# CHANGELOG-ARCHIVE.md (kept so CHANGELOG.md's link to it resolves), CONTRIBUTING.md
# Exclude everything else — internal docs, tools, test infra, plugin configs
exclude = [
    # Plugin / IDE configs
    ".claude/",
    ".claude-plugin/",
    ".codex-plugin/",
    ".factory-plugin/",
    ".serena/",
    ".playwright-mcp/",
    ".playwright-cli/",
    ".github/",
    ".lore/",
    ".internal/",
    # Directories not needed in package.
    #
    # ANCHORED WITH A LEADING SLASH. Unanchored, these match a directory of
    # that name at ANY depth — "agents/" also matched src/llm_router/agents/
    # and stripped it from the sdist. `uv build` builds the WHEEL FROM THE
    # SDIST, so the published wheel was missing the package too, and
    # `import llm_router.server` failed with
    # "No module named 'llm_router.agents'".
    #
    # It shipped that way in 13.0.0. A local `uv build --wheel` builds straight
    # from source and included the files, so every pre-release check passed —
    # the only thing that would have caught it is installing the published
    # artifact, which is why that step exists.
    #
    # llm_router.agents.session is also in server._CRITICAL_MODULES, so the
    # server refuses to start rather than degrading.
    "/agents/",
    "/demo/",
    "/docs/",
    "/research/",
    "/deprecation/",
    "/scripts/",
    "/skills/",
    "/submissions/",
    "/tests/",
    # The quarantine lives at the repo ROOT, not under tests/, so the "/tests/"
    # entry never covered it and 13.0.2 shipped 16 files of dead, uncollectable
    # test code to PyPI. Same anchoring lesson as the block above, inverted:
    # there the pattern matched too much, here it matched too little.
    "/_quarantined_tests/",
    # Test dirs that are NOT at the repo root-level tests/. "/tests/" is anchored
    # to the root, so it never covered these two; sdist shipped
    # integrations/pi/tests/* and src/llm_router/mods/llm-router-receipt/tests/
    # band.test.ts (test_sdist_does_not_ship_the_active_test_suite, slow-marked,
    # so CI never ran it). Listed by exact path, not an unanchored "tests/",
    # because that would also match any package dir of that name under src/.
    "/integrations/pi/tests/",
    "/src/llm_router/mods/llm-router-receipt/tests/",
    "/awesome-readme/",
    # Research/eval working data at the repo ROOT. `src/llm_router/data/` is
    # package data and MUST stay — hence the leading slash, per the anchoring
    # lesson above.
    #
    # Caught by building the sdist before tagging: /data/policy/embed_cache.jsonl
    # alone is 224 MB, which took the 13.2.0 sdist to 101 MB compressed — over
    # PyPI's 100 MB per-file limit. The upload would have failed, or worse
    # succeeded and permanently shipped a RouterArena embedding cache to everyone
    # who installs the router.
    "/data/",
    "/experiments/",
    # Hypothesis's local example database — per-machine test state, never
    # something an installer needs.
    "/.hypothesis/",
    # Scratch files that accumulate at the repo root during development. They are
    # untracked, so git never complains, and nothing but an sdist listing reveals
    # that they were about to be published.
    "/test_uploads_task_func/",
    "/file1.txt",
    "/file2.jpg",
    "/file_sizes.csv",
    "/files.zip",
    "/prefix_42.json",
    "/test_server.csv",
    "/test_server_structured.csv",
    # ── Backup / temp files — never publish (CLAUDE.md sdist safety rule) ─
    ".env.backup.*",
    "*.bak",
    "*.bak.*",
    # Private / internal docs — never publish
    "CLAUDE.md",
    "MONETIZATION.md",
    "ROADMAP.md",
    "STRATEGY.md",
    "PRICING.md",
    "SECURITY.md",
    "PHASE_COMPLETION_REVIEW.md",
    # Build / deploy artifacts
    "Dockerfile",
    "Procfile",
    "uv.lock",
    "mcp.json",
    ".mcp.json",
    # Images
    "*.png",
    "*.jpg",
    # Git metadata not needed in package
    ".gitignore",
    ".gitattributes",
    # Broken directory from gitignore quoting
    '"/Users/',
    '"/',
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Quarantined by the 13.0.0 sync — see tests/_downstream_legacy/README.md.
# Excluded from collection rather than deleted: each still describes behaviour
# somebody tested, and the decision to drop that coverage is a human one.
# The quarantine lives at the repo ROOT (_quarantined_tests/), not under
# tests/, so nothing that scans the test tree has to know about it. It was
# inside tests/ first and the mutation-scope generator walked straight into
# it, deriving an exclusion set that named quarantined files.
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"
timeout = 30
filterwarnings = [
    # aiosqlite's worker thread may attempt call_soon_threadsafe after the
    # session-scoped event loop is torn down by pytest-asyncio.
    "ignore:Exception in thread.*_connection_worker_thread:pytest.PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning",
]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"' for fast feedback)",
    "fast: marks tests as fast (run with '-m fast' for quick validation)",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests (slow external calls)",
    "requires_ollama: marks tests that require local Ollama instance (skip in CI)",
    "requires_api_keys: marks tests that require mocked API keys (skip in CI)",
    "requires_codex: marks tests that require Codex availability (skip in CI)",
    "e2e: end-to-end: real boundaries, not doubles",
    "mcp_handshake: MCP protocol handshake conformance",
    "performance: latency/throughput measurement, not correctness",
    "routing_hermetic: routing with every external call stubbed",
    "timing: pass/fail depends on wall-clock speed (elapsed/p95/loop-lag/short real timeouts/sleep ordering); excluded from the parallel CI job and run serially by the `timing` job (TIMING-1)",
]
addopts = "-m 'not slow and not requires_ollama and not requires_api_keys and not requires_codex' -q --tb=short"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"  # matches requires-python = ">=3.11"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Pin rule selection explicitly (pre-0.16 ruff defaults) so unpinned `uvx ruff`
# upgrades in CI cannot change lint behavior (0.16.1 broadened defaults and
# introduced ~1,455 new findings with zero code changes).
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F"]
